evals.prompt: /grill-me I'm planning to split our monolithic bmcweb patch series (14 commits) into three separate Gerrit topics so reviewers can approve them independently.
evals.expected_output: The skill delegates to a grilling session: one question at a time with a recommended answer, no action taken.
expectations: Runs a grilling-style interview (equivalent to the /grilling skill) rather than giving a one-shot critique or list of concerns
Asks a single question in the response
Gives a recommended answer for that question
Does not restructure commits or touch Gerrit

evals.prompt: /grill-me Design: a local cache for repo sync mirrors shared over NFS across 4 build servers, so each server doesn't re-fetch from upstream.
evals.expected_output: A relentless, sequential interview on the cache design, starting with a high-leverage decision and recommending an answer.
expectations: Asks only one question at a time
Each question is paired with the agent's recommended answer
The first question addresses a decision other choices depend on (e.g. concurrency/locking on NFS, mirror freshness, failure mode when NFS is down)
Does not propose a full design document or implementation before the user confirms shared understanding

evals.prompt: /grill-me My plan for next sprint: rewrite the gerrit-ci-retrigger skill's report.py in Go for speed.
evals.expected_output: The agent grills the plan, looking up checkable facts itself (e.g. what report.py does, where time goes) and only asking the user about decisions.
expectations: Looks up (or states it will look up) facts about report.py from the filesystem rather than asking the user what the script does
Asks a single decision question, not several
Includes a recommended answer with that question
Does not begin rewriting the script
